topics.name: Adverbs of manner, time and frequency
Modals can / could / may / must / should

options: The moon go round the earth.
The moon going round the earth.
The moon goes round the earth.
questions.rule: A universal fact takes the simple present. The moon is singular: goes.

options: Bhikhu drinked a glass of milk.
Bhikhu drank a glass of milk.
Bhikhu drunk a glass of milk.
questions.rule: drink is irregular: drink - drank - drunk. The simple past is drank.
After should use the base verb: should wake.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A scientific fact takes the simple present, and water is singular: boils.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Yesterday needs the past. bring - brought.
tomorrow is the future: will + base verb.
wakes shows a present habit, so a frequency adverb like always fits; yesterday and tomorrow clash with the present.
Subject + verb + adverb: The farmer works very hard.

chat: What did you do last Sunday?
options: I weared my new shoes to a wedding.
I wore my new shoes to a wedding.
I worn my new shoes to a wedding.
questions.rule: wear is irregular: wear - wore - worn.
Simple future: will + base verb: will visit.

options: The woodcutter finded a bag of gold.
The woodcutter find a bag of gold yesterday.
The woodcutter found a bag of gold.
questions.rule: find is irregular: find - found.

options: Meera often goes to the library.
Meera often going to the library.
Meera often go to the library.
questions.rule: Frequency adverb before the main verb, and Meera takes goes: often goes.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After should not use the base verb: should not waste.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To describe how he worked, use adverbs: lazily and slowly.
Last year needs the simple past: begin - began - begun.
A fact of nature takes the simple present. The moon is singular: appears.
Subject + must not + base verb: We must not waste time.
forgive - forgave: Grandma forgave me for the mistake.
A habit takes the simple present I practise. every is followed by a singular noun: every evening.

chat: I have a test tomorrow, but I want to watch a movie.
options: You should revising first and watch the movie later.
You should to revise first and watch the movie later.
You should revise first and watch the movie later.
questions.rule: Give advice with should + base verb: should revise. No to after should.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: Yesterday I eat an apple, and tomorrow I will eat a mango.
Yesterday I ate an apple, and tomorrow I will ate a mango.
Yesterday I ate an apple, and tomorrow I will eat a mango.
questions.rule: Yesterday takes the past ate; tomorrow takes will + base verb: will eat.

options: Bhikhu knew about the gold but did not go.
Bhikhu knowed about the gold but did not go.
Bhikhu knew about the gold but did not went.
questions.rule: know - knew. After did not use the base verb: did not go.

options: The woodcutter could not believe his eyes.
The woodcutter could not believed his eyes.
The woodcutter could not believes his eyes.
questions.rule: could is already past; the verb after it stays in the base form: could not believe.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Simple future: will + base verb: will learn.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To say how he spoke, use the adverb kindly, not the adjective kind.
A word describing an action is an adverb: quickly cut down.
Advice: should not + base verb. are keep and you does are wrong forms.
Simple future: subject + will + base verb: We will win the next match.

chat: Did you see the sunrise this morning?
options: Yes, I seen it from the terrace.
Yes, I seed it from the terrace.
Yes, I saw it from the terrace.
questions.rule: see - saw - seen. The simple past is saw.

chat: Does your teacher give homework every day?
options: Yes, she give us homework every day.
Yes, she gives us homework every day.
Yes, she is give us homework every day.
questions.rule: A daily habit takes the simple present. she takes gives.

options: The farmer was a honest and hardworking man.
The farmer was an honest and hardworking man.
The farmer were an honest and hardworking man.
questions.rule: honest starts with a vowel sound, so use an. One farmer takes was.

options: The children brought many mangoes from the farm.
The children bringed many mangoes from the farm.
The childrens brought many mangoes from the farm.
questions.rule: bring - brought. children is already plural; no extra s.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: sleep is irregular: sleep - slept.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Comparing how two people did something needs the adverb: more quickly than.

questions.after: late, so he never sees the sunrise.
questions.rule: A habit with always and sees is in the simple present: wakes up.

questions.after: find the gold because the woodcutter had taken it home.
questions.rule: Inability in the past: could not. The next day is in the past, so cannot is wrong.
Past question: Wh- word + did + subject + base verb: Why did Bhikhu lose the gold?
When Who is the subject, use the past verb directly: Who wore ...?

options: Yes, you mays. Please return it after the class.
Yes, you may. Please returns it after the class.
Yes, you may. Please return it after the class.
questions.rule: Modals never add s: you may. A request uses the base verb: Please return.

chat: Did you finish your science project?
options: Not yet. I will finish it tonight.
Not yet. I will finished it tonight.
Not yet. I finishing it tonight.
questions.rule: A plan for later uses will + base verb: will finish.

options: When the rain comes, the white lily blossoms, and when the rain goes, the lily disappears too.
When the rain comes, the white lily blossom, and when the rain goes, the lily disappears too.
When the rain comes, the white lily blossoms, and when the rain go, the lily disappears too.
questions.rule: Every singular subject in the present needs -s: rain comes, lily blossoms, rain goes.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct past forms.
options: Bhikhu begun the day late, drank his tea slowly and forgot all about the gold.
Bhikhu began the day late, drunk his tea slowly and forgot all about the gold.
Bhikhu began the day late, drank his tea slowly and forgot all about the gold.
questions.rule: Simple past forms: began, drank, forgot. begun and drunk need has/had.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: All three actions are in the past: cut, found, took.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After must use the base verb: must work.

questions.after: only once, when the rain comes.
questions.rule: Every year and comes show a present fact. The lily is singular: blossoms.

questions.after: bends the branches of the tall trees.
questions.rule: The word tells how the breeze bends, so use the adverb gently.
Frequency adverb never goes before the main verb: Bhikhu never saw the sunrise.
Question with a modal: Wh- word + should + subject + base verb.

chat: What did you learn from the story of the lazy son?
options: I learnt that we should never putting off our work.
I learnt that we should never put off our work.
I learnt that we should never puts off our work.
questions.rule: After should never use the base verb: should never put off.

chat: Will you come cycling with me at six tomorrow morning?
options: Sure! I will set an alarm, so I won't overslept.
Sure! I will set an alarm, so I won't oversleep.
Sure! I will sets an alarm, so I won't oversleep.
questions.rule: will and won't are followed by the base verb: will set, won't oversleep.
